moat_against: Asset-based fees are hostage to market levels — a bear market cuts AUM/AUA revenue with no action by SEIC
Fee pressure across asset management and administration; larger custody banks (BNY, State Street) and SS&C compete on scale
ROIC proxy is falling — 42.4% in FY2021 to 24.0% in FY2025 — as the Stratos acquisition swells goodwill/intangibles and invested capital
Growth is historically modest — 5-yr revenue CAGR 6.4% — and the recent acceleration is partly inorganic (Stratos, closed Dec 2025) and market appreciation
Client concentration / mandate-loss risk — large platform relationships can unwind on a client's own strategic change
moat_for: SEI Wealth Platform is deeply embedded back/middle-office infrastructure — migration cost and operational risk make switching rare
Recurring revenue base — asset-based and processing fees on ~$2.1T managed/advised/administered assets (Q2 2026)
Returns through a cycle — ROIC proxy 24-43% over FY2016-25, never below 24%, gross margin rising to 35.2% in FY2025 and 36.0% TTM
Asset-light, net-cash model — capex ~1% of revenue, SBC only ~8-9% of OCF, buybacks shrinking diluted shares 2.6%/yr
moat_justification: Moderate-strong narrow moat: the SEI Wealth Platform and investment-manager outsourcing are mission-critical, deeply embedded systems with high switching costs and a largely recurring, asset-based fee base, evidenced by a ROIC proxy that stayed between 24% and 43% over FY2016-25 (30.4% in FY2024, 24.0% in FY2025) and gross margin expanding from 29.0% in FY2023 to 35.2% in FY2025 / 36.0% TTM. Capped at 6, not 7+: ROIC is trending down as Stratos goodwill/intangibles swell invested capital, revenue growth averaged only 6.4% over five years, fees carry full equity-market beta, and custody-bank/SS&C scale competitors contest every mandate — pricing power is real but not structural.
name: SEI Investments Company
one_liner: High-quality asset-light platform compounder, moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% at $104.40 (weighted IRR 10.3%, weighted IV@15% $62.41); it clears 15% only at ~$62, so the quality is not the debate, the price is.
